dimensions.assessment: Affects current and former Members of Congress, along with their survivors or beneficiaries.
dimensions.evidence: An individual who is or was a Member of Congress, or the survivor or beneficiary of such individual, may not be paid annuity or retired pay

dimensions.assessment: The financial effect of losing retirement pay or annuities is major for the individuals affected.
dimensions.evidence: prohibit pay of annuity or retired pay to a Member of Congress convicted of a criminal offense committed during congressional service

dimensions.assessment: Reduces federal spending on individual congressional pensions under specified circumstances, but the overall fiscal effect is negligible relative to the federal budget.
Amends chapter 83 of title 5, United States Code, to add specific statutory restrictions on congressional pension eligibility.
dimensions.evidence: To amend chapter 83 of title 5, United States Code, to prohibit pay of annuity or retired pay to a Member of Congress

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change affecting all future applicable convictions, determinations, and terminations beginning with the next succeeding Congress.
dimensions.evidence: This section shall take effect on the date on which the next succeeding Congress begins after the date of the enactment of this section

missing_information: The exact number of Members of Congress or beneficiaries who might be affected is not stated.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill prohibits federal annuity or retired pay for Members of Congress convicted of certain criminal offenses or determined to have engaged in sexual conduct with subordinate officers or employees. The population affected is limited to current and former Members of Congress and their survivors or beneficiaries.
